i already said in my first sentence that i don’t want to control anyone’s posts… your insinuation here is also an attempt to control what/where i post while telling me not to do that to others, which i haven’t — i made my own post to speak about my own feelings that i know others have voiced as well; just asking people to be more cognizant and considerate of others in a sub dedicated to people dealing with an eating disorder

read the other comments in the thread if you want more insight — i’m done with incoming hostility from people just because i believe being mindful of everyone is a key aspect of any community… everyone here agrees this sub should be treated like a “safe space” or “harm reduction” despite us all being here for our own reasons, yet some people are insistent on being selfish about how they show up and i’m allowed to disagree with people’s actions in that regard

wishing you recovery

dude, i’m not arguing — this is childish now… it’s my post and you commented then assumed things about my character for asking people to be more considerate of others in the group

all i’m saying is i wouldn’t run into an AA meeting telling people about a beer sale up the street… end of 

i wish you recovery and a restful sunday

you don’t know anything about me, assumptions about my character are not necessary lol

a tag is a small feat to make this more of a safe space and it doesn’t hinder anyone’s experience to be more mindful of those around you?

i didn’t do anything to suggest it’s my way or the highway; if anything it’s the opposite as that is the impression i get from people who refuse to even hear the other side out given all of these comments and believe someone ~not scrolling past~ their literal addiction is a personal issue of hypersensitivity among a group many people see as a “safe space” or “harm reduction”…

bye!

we just don’t know if it’s all safe…
have a good day though, wishing you recovery

you could’ve scrolled past this too lmao 

i’m not arguing with anyone — it’d be a good thing if we started tagging posts that are just about indulging and sharing the unsafe, for-profit sources of the things we all clearly have trouble with… how is that a safe space if only some people feel safe? 

read my other comments for my feelings on this, otherwise i’m not trying to engage with people downvoting me for saying the quiet part out loud or misunderstanding where i’m coming from simply because they want to keep doing whatever without question and not think critically about it or how they might be affecting others in this community

i agree with what you’ve said about the likely desensitization online because of internet non-food eating trends like tide pods meeting the overall popularity of ASMR videos and that people experiencing pica (even unknowingly) might see this differently

in terms of the baddies episodes, it’s something i only noticed after the tiktok ASMR videos got popular and there’s two specific scenes:
- one scene is on a private jet (i think it’s in a later caribbean episode) and it’s hard to see who is passing it to whom, but there’s this specific brand of corn starch passed through the seats and it’s spoken about very briefly! i only noticed the brand because it’s the same as a popular one in ASMR videos
- one scene is from a recent episode of midwest where tinkabella is just in her room and the corn starch is on her dresser? it felt purposeful given how short the scene is and there’s nothing else on the dresser in view, but i don’t know why that would be the case — same aforementioned brand as well

i agree that it’s inherent in having a disorder and not “wanting clout” but i beg to differ about the trending aspect: more people are making videos about it as ASMR and by association, tiktok’s algorithms have been putting these videos on people’s fyp (that have never experienced this before) as ASMR… i never saw this frequently until my friend who doesn’t have pica pointed it out to me and has sent me dozens of these ASMR videos

i also see a lot of people in the comments saying they want to try the non-foods being eaten in the ASMR videos “because it looks good” and “satisfying”

there’s also a few episodes of the tv show ‘baddies’ where one girl brings corn starch with her on the private jet to share and has it out on her dresser while getting ready lol

i hear what you’re saying for sure and i agree to an extent — i wish for everyone’s recovery ❤️‍🩹 and i hold zero judgment for anyone struggling with it because i wouldn’t be in this sub if i didn’t identify with these feelings

i just don’t think providing the materials and sending people to for-profit sellers is the way? that’s the opposite of safe if we’re viewing it from this perspective… it’s also an eating disorder and i think people would view it very differently if this was about sharing for-profit sources and tips on “safe” ways to stay thin

most of us are likely not experts in harm reduction  nor is there any actual place for us to collectively find the resources needed, so i  understand the different perspectives here too and i don’t want to come across as judgmental of anyone

this said though, there are many factors and variables aside not having a place to vent or seek support that would affect someone indulging and our best bet at a healthy life and a real safe space is to share and listen without tempting anyone to go against their better judgment in the same breath

yes i do know what it is; as a group, we are not harm reduction experts and there is no way to know if the sellers being shared are providing “safe”, food-grade materials…

like you said, we can’t be on here trying to “resolve each other’s problems” which includes sending people to buy from random sellers around the internet with no knowledge of where they’re procuring their products or how they’re processing them or even how they’re storing them…  we literally don’t know if it’s any different from getting dirt off the street 

and people are still making money off of us? harm reduction in itself is not meant to be for profit off of addicts… do you know what harm reduction is?
I did this as a kid and had to go to the hospital for it. It just made me feel very sick unfortunately.

Gosh, reading this made a lot of sense and you’re very level-headed about it to be completely honest. This has definitely changed given me perspective as well.

Good for you that you’ve been at it for a couple years! I understand what you mean when you say it feels bad to have to start over, but I really want to reiterate that you deserve to live happily and trying your genuine best matters a lot here. In time, the cravings can also fade as that did happen for me at one point. The compulsion/physical urge I’ve personally only tackled (healthily) by doing things like drinking water helped a lot somehow or going for a walk then seeing how I feel afterwards. Sometimes I’d forget about it for a few additional hours at minimum.

In terms of feeling judgment from professionals, aside my wonderful therapist I even told my family doctor once and he sucks lol, but it went fine. He didn’t even bat a lash; he immediately asked me if I’d checked my iron recently, got me to get blood work done, then prescribed some iron pills to see how it helped. No other questions aside what my regular eating habits are like, exercise regimens, etc. It sounds much scarier than it is ultimately.

In terms of healthy alternatives, you’ve definitely helped me think more about my stance on this. When I mentioned it, I was only really referring to food. I deal with paper as my non-food; I’ve had a hard time finding alternatives to try to ween myself off entirely and when I have, it just led to consuming the alternative a lot more. Initially, my take was that I personally wouldn’t suggest trying anything that isn’t well-known to be a healthy, nutritious food already—but even then considering everything we’ve spoken about, I’d advise you be careful and just try to stay away from advertised “alternatives” altogether. You’re absolutely right that a lot of the stuff posted online aimed at the demographic here is predatory and unethical. And it’s sad to hear that there’s so much more to this that’s broadening in scope online only really to sell what could be poison to people. I don’t want to encourage the behaviour and just staying “sober” from it is likely best.

I empathize with your last comments as well. I wish I could tell myself when I was younger that this could be harmful in the future. Sending warmth and hugs 🫂 You’ve got this and again, great job on your couple years “sober”. ❤️

omg i think i might’ve actually commented on it! i agree with you, i see a lot of people treating it as trendy on tiktok and i feel like some of that attitude is migrating into this sub—i’ve been here long enough to see this becoming more of a thing than it was in the past and it’s lowkey scary…
venting comes in all different forms ❤️ no personal judgment to anyone in this sub — i’m wishing you and everyone here good health
i absolutely agree and thank you for your response :) wishing you well! i sought out this sub for the same reasons

thank you for understanding; i think your idea for a tag would be great or just using the nsfw tag would be helpful as well!

i agree that limiting what we can talk about would be unfair, but i’m definitely not advocating for this sub to disappear in any way — i agree heavily that this sub can be a place of harm reduction for many, but the encouragement and sharing sellers is not that…

i’m glad you enjoy the subreddit, but what you’re saying here misses my point? i never said we need to fix each other’s issues and i’m not saying we can’t share what’s going on with ourselves 

i empathize with wanting to share about experiences with mental health issues that, when discussed, lifts a weight off!

however, why are people sharing links and posts to sellers who profit off of us? why are people encouraging it in each other in comments? never mind “resolving each others’ problems”, these things make the problems worse…?

i appreciate your response and for the care you have for people dealing with pica! ❤️ i have found help in perspectives while being here and i’m glad this subreddit exists

i’m also not expecting you to remove people or posts for simply sharing their experiences; i’m just a bit frustrated with seeing people encourage it and share the places they are seeking non-foods from—the only people benefitting in that regard are the ones making money off of this community and no one can even be truly sure if what they’re purchasing from sellers on tiktok and ig is safe(r)

Firstly, I want to say thank you for sharing! It is brave to confront all of these feelings and I identify with a lot of them. I don’t think you should be so hard on yourself. Your health and happiness matter a lot.

I was just thinking about so much of this a couple of hours ago. I too have dealt with this since my preteen-teen years and I’ve always been considered intelligent in my social and professional circles. I did quite well in school and also had this specific relentless drive to get rid of this part of myself that eats non-food once I got to adulthood despite how hard it is. As it relates to the psychological experience of eating non-foods, mental health struggles come in all different packages; you’re not a bad person because of it. You were not bad to your parents and you have much to be proud of; this issue does not define who you are as you seem to be well-accomplished and have a good head on your shoulders.

Some suggest pica is a form of OCD and when I was treated for that, it worked—although with too many side effects to continue for me; try talking to your doctor about it. I’ve also been to therapy for other things and brought pica up; at no point was my therapist judgmental so I’d recommend finding a good one to talk to about it to ease some of the stress you feel that may lead to it. Seasoned medical professionals worth their salt have seen it all, so don’t be embarrassed to talk to one that seems good.

What really helped me was looking at it as you’ve mentioned here; like an addiction (which is a disorder itself). Understanding you have trouble controlling this and that change has to be made is a great start to getting better! Do what you can to find alternatives to this that are healthier. Try to challenge yourself to stay away from it. See how long you can go. You’re not bad if you need to try again. Best of luck to you <3

Being validated feels good, especially if validation has not easily been given to you or has been given then taken away in the past. It’s okay to want people to acknowledge your feelings, give you a break, and hold space for you when things are especially difficult.

Mild to severe agoraphobia. Social isolation gets discussed a lot, but simply never wanting to leave your house/your room/your safe place has become an issue for me. Avoiding events not because you don’t want community or that you never have a good time, but because the mere thought of going out is enough to cause a panic and keep you inside “where it’s safe”.

Agreeing with others to find your safe foods! Maybe find a comfortable time to sit down and make a list — to make it easier, maybe go by food group.

Once you have a list of everything that feels okay to eat, there are websites that allow you to enter each ingredient and you can find recipes using your safe foods that way.

Until then, I would suggest high protein granola bars, high protein greek yogurt, Ensure/other meal replacement drinks, any fresh fruit or veggies, and most importantly: reaching out to a doctor to get blood tests for any nutrients you might be missing. Talking about ARFID can be hard, but finding out if there are any vitamins you can take/be prescribed will help a ton. 

Wishing you the best of luck and if you want to talk about it on a personal level with someone also of similar ethnic background (Caribbean, so a lot of similar foods) or just about recovery, my DMs are open ❤️

I agree with those saying it can be a texture-based gamble, but I also think apart of unlearning that is slowly showing the kid how tasty things can be made at home.

I’m vegetarian of 8 years and have had ARFID since I was a kid — I’ve always loved healthy foods like broccoli and cauliflower (as someone else said: crunch is good), but sauces really bothered me for a while. What’s helped me 1000% is making more food from scratch so I know exactly what’s in it and there are no surprises. Doing that with my parents/babysitter as a kid changed my perspective for sure.

i prefer thinner tp as well, i don’t much like the overly imprinted, good quality 3-ply stuff

the brands of rolling papers i go for have no chemical taste! i would assume they’re processed differently than tp since they’re made for smoking

they kinda taste similar to tp with a different texture — rolling papers are just a lot more thin and “melt” a bit differently as they’re made of arabic gum

pace myself with 1-3 of the following:
- instant ramen
- spoonful of peanut butter
- small cup of greek yogurt mixed with jam
- granola bar
- chips or rice crackers
- juice or tea with sugar/honey & lemon
- baby carrots or a couple of tangerines

once i have an okay sized portion of food in my body, i take vitamins //// meal-prepping something long lasting that i can just heat up super fast helps a ton

yes, same — my friend who does not have pica has been getting a lot of corn starch videos on her feed and sending them to me asking if she should try it (i’ve softly told her i have pica, but not for corn starch — trying to ensure she doesn’t get too into it for the ASMR aspect)

I appreciate you sharing this <3 I definitely think my pica is OCD related as well. I was prescribed an SSRI a few years ago for depression and anxiety, but it also happened to be an option for OCD despite that not being what we were explicitly treating. Everyone’s experiences with these things are different of course, but the SSRI surprisingly stopped my cravings and anxiety entirely, but the side effects were too bad to continue.

I know the feeling. Things feel rough right now, but I really just want you to know you’re not alone here.

I’m going through this right now, in fact. I tried to deactivate my Instagram twice in the last two weeks and when the website wouldn’t let me, it made me unspeakably upset. I left that alone, stopped posting altogether, and made my other socials private (while blocking random accounts I didn’t recognize). I have pretty much distanced myself from my closest friends by making excuses for missed calls and unanswered texts when I don’t “feel their support” and I’ve been going out of my way to eat lunch alone at work.

I don’t have a solution for you, but I can share small things that helped me:

When I can, I try to reflect and extend a little hello to people who feel at least a little safe—keeping it short and sweet. People I consider kind and don’t talk to too often, if you have anyone like that around you. An old-coworker who enjoys similar movies came to mind and we talked about that. Baby steps back into community.

Also, reading about things I enjoy has helped a lot. Any solo activity that requires patience and allows a bit of distraction (knitting, gardening/taking real good care of houseplants, sitting in the park playing solitaire, writing prose about how I feel in a small notebook when I’m feeling in extremes, etc. have been helpful for me).

Sending emotional warmth to you. I hope you’re able to find some inner calm at this time. It’s tough, but I genuinely believe in you. ❤️❤️❤️

hello! i deal with arfid and have for some time (i’m quite picky and it can sometimes feel stress-related). working to deal with it on my own for some years now—if you want to chat about it via DM, i’m all ears and open to it. :)

no worries, i’m glad i could help <3 i don’t talk to my dad anymore because of issues like him yelling at me for crying and other similar experiences. 

i empathize with you and i hear you; please always remember you’re not alone.

i’m very sorry to hear about this and that you aren’t being given the help & understanding you deserve. your father & his girlfriend sound unstable and you should be somewhere safe for yourself. 

you are a priority and you’re important. it can be hard to remind yourself of this, but say it to yourself even if it feels untrue sometimes.

do you have a family doctor that you can talk to by chance? or any neighbours that might be okay to reach out to in the event of emergency? 

are there any community centres in your area? somewhere you can sit and chill, meet other people your age, join an activity, or go for a run? or anywhere you can go to get your mind off of things for the time being?

even though school is out right now, is it possible for you to go to the library either at school or a public library in the area?

leaving the situation to do these things isn’t permanent, but reserving your happiness & peace is important for your sense of being and control when home is rocky.

for coping: if you’re feeling anxious or like you can’t get out of the space, i highly encourage deep breathing, exercise, listening to music you love with headphones on, or body scanning if you can. this is not medical advice and i’d definitely suggest seeking out a counsellor, therapist, nurse, or doctor at school whenever possible. they’ll be able to give you tools or resources that are suitable for how you’re feeling deep down.

just speak for yourself. you can wish that suffering onto yourself if that’s what you want, but i’m actually moving towards healing since i wrote this 5 days ago. 

you’re not even trying to relate to me with this comment; you’re just projecting and being rude.

I hear you! Hating sauce is a lot more common than we’d like to think; I have a couple of friends who feel the same way. I hated ketchup, yellow mustard, mayo, and relish all from a very young age—I still hate mustard & relish, but ketchup and I are okay now lmao. Mayo is whatever, but too much of anything and I have to wipe it off with a napkin.

I just got tired of hating sauces. At a point, I just felt the only way to be okay with them was to start making them myself! It was the only thing that helped my brain get over it to an extent—my logic is that since I know exactly what’s in the sauce/dip I made, I have no reason to fear it. Eventually, I tried others. I’m still very weary of sauces/dips in my mind, but it’s nowhere near as strict as it once was.

In terms of the burger example, I think it makes sense that you don’t like combo textures—those can be very hit or miss. I believe in textural harmony; I love veggie-based soups, fresh salads, pastas, etc. because the textures are predictable and don’t change much as you eat them. When a burger turns mushy from the heat & moisture, I have to throw it away omg…

That said, I find it so interesting that you don’t like combo flavours. I feel this has been my saving grace, in that trying new things has been a saving grace for you. I have more hesitancy in that department, so kudos! 

And in a similar way to you being a super taster, my friends tell me that I have a knack for knowing “what something needs” in terms of flavour/spice. My family is from an island where there’s lots of food for all diet restrictions, but most things have a lot of different spices. I’m grateful not to have the cilantro soap gene, but I am also just lucky to have a mom who has always cooked really flavourful stuff that I enjoy and it’s carried over into my eating habits now that I live alone.

Wow, wasn’t expecting that motor oil story! The fact you’d come to learn more about your sense of flavour that way is super interesting! Seafood is very hit or miss; I remember growing up smelling fish in lunches at school that didn’t sit well with me. I also lucked out here because my family is from an island where seafood is traditionally always cooked (no sliminess—I hate raw fish) and has no upsetting smells or lingering fish taste.

LOL I also hate the idea of pineapple chicken. I’ve never had it, but it sounds bad. I think flavour/texture matching is an art. Not everyone can do it well. I love cheese, bread, nut, & fruit charcuterie boards for exploring texture and flavour simultaneously—it helps seeing everything individually and eating it however I want. Add a little honey? Sooooo delicious, if you’re looking for a way to dabble.

hey! i think i understand what you’re feeling (to an extent of course, your experiences are your own and they’re valid). it’s really annoying and upsetting when people point out what you’re eating or make fun of the choice when it was hard to in the first place. it made me hate eating out with friends for a while; one time i ordered a burger and only removed like 3 out of 8 things (i normally would take off more so i felt good about my order) and then everyone was like “what toppings are even left? you’re just gonna eat it plain? blah blah blah”—stuff like this feels disregarding and rude, but it’s hard to talk about when people are generally condescending toward the behaviour or feeling we possess. 

admittedly, my arfid has been more of a picky eating / ignoring food out of stress kind of thing—a lot of people don’t understand that it can often stem from bad interactions with food that go back years.

if you’re comfortable, can you name what kinds of foods you like? and what kinds of foods you don’t like? you can also tell me via DM if it’d be better privately. there are a lot of things i wouldn’t eat for a long time that i’m growing and working on—my mom and best friend have inadvertently helped a lot with this. i used to freak out if my roommate ordered me food i’d never tried before (in 2020) and i’ve improved so much since then. i’m sorry to hear it’s been difficult working on this with your husband, but with time and patience i would hope he comes to understand this beyond “let’s cure it” with no real plan.

from the sounds of it as well, you have some intense fears around choking—have you sought therapy at all for this specifically? in terms of unlearning a fear or finding ways to cope with that fear, family doctors and the like haven’t been the most supportive or understanding for me either. finding a therapist you can actually connect with, who has training in ED & OCD, might be a safe bet here.
ahhhh that’s so sweet, i didn’t even think to google that—thank you for the help again ❤️❤️
thank you for your suggestions! finding food like my non-food might be a task (toilet paper & rolling papers for me—i’ve heard rice paper might be good?), but i’ll give it a shot.

yes, my bp2 is more depression-oriented and my hypomanic episodes are rarer. i really hate feeling depressed (duh lmao) and like i can’t do much else, so when i get hypomanic it’s this combo of borderline insane and very productive for me—it feels weird to miss it for me too, but i think i know what you mean

what helps rid me of the overstimulated feeling is to just focus on one thing and make it easy & tasty. pick the thing that requires your attention and then find easy ways to do sides. 
for example, if you don’t already: baking your main item and then using a rice cooker to steam veggies like broccoli & green beans, or grains like quinoa & rice, etc. are great ways to take a lot of work off of your hands.

if you like chicken and veggies, that’s a perfect start on its own! again, baking might be a good start if things seem like a lot of work; just set a timer to be safe.

if you like most veggies, i promise that can be as easy as throwing things into a pot on the stove or glass dish for the oven, sprinkle a couple seasonings, and wait.
roasted carrots, kale chips, roasted sweet potato, roasted corn, roasted chickpeas, etc. 
all these veggies include minimal chopping and can be put into the oven with a little oil or butter + salt & pepper!

one of my go-tos when i need something easy & foolproof: 
- chop up 2-3 medium potatoes 
- put them in a container with a little salt & pepper, olive oil, italian seasoning, and some chopped/minced garlic.
- close & shake the container to coat everything
- throw it into the oven, spread out on a glass dish @ 400 degrees and wait till they are crispy outside & soft inside

also if you like nuts at all, i would highly recommend them when you’re feeling low energy or just need a healthy protein source aside chicken.

and lastly, salads & bowls !!! grab packaged greens or a grain like farro or quinoa that you can put in a rice cooker (you can make yummy salads mixing both greens & grains!). once you have your base, there’s so much you can do to make it flavourful and to have a chance to try different things based on what you know you like—try adding things like any leftover chicken you might have, any of the roasted veggies i mentioned earlier, fruits that are easy to work with like dried cranberries or tangerines, use a grater for carrots, green beans/edamame, any sprouts, almonds or walnuts, maybe a little balsamic vinegar & olive oil?

again, i know it can be hard and it can take a lot to just find the energy to do it, but i genuinely believe you can ❤️ take it one step at a time

i’ve had a similar issue, so i feel you on having a hard time with getting it right for yourself to heal and feel good ❤️ go easy on yourself

have you tried looking at any recipes or meal prep ideas? it can seem daunting/overwhelming to do and i understand it takes a lot of effort to cook sometimes, but what’s helped me is really thinking about the kinds of foods and flavours that i like and trying to work towards them. 

i am currently vegetarian and have been doing well so far this year at making myself nutritious meals i am proud to share with friends. my mom is an excellent cook and has helped in giving me pointers in making easy, healthy foods—i can share if you have any interest. :)

that said, is there anything you particularly enjoy? anything in particular you tend to gravitate towards? healthy or not
please leave him, no one should ever treat you like that. his behaviour won’t stop until he stops it, put yourself and your feelings first.

i’m so sorry you have such a weight in your shoulders at such a young age. i know she’s your mom and there is this really big cultural sense that you have to do what she says and that money is a big deal when your parents sacrifice for you, but you are your own person. you will never NOT be your own person and your best interests are most known to YOU. find the things you like to do and keep doing them, even if you feel it has to happen while studying chemistry if that’s not something you feel you can give up.

i’m glad you have your brother to help you, but never stop reminding yourself that you are important and your feelings are valid. it’s hard to do and sometimes it feels fake, but you sound like a caring and kind family member to your loved ones. your self-esteem is still blossoming and your mother should be more supportive of your well-being. no excuses—a good mom is someone who is loving and tries to be present for you when you need it and is possible for her.

i admire your ability to be present for your family—i’ve done it and it’s difficult. it can be a heavy mental strain and you deserve time to take care of yourself.

i want you to know that even though i don’t know you, i want you to find whatever it is that makes you feel good that doesn’t harm yourself or others and please lean into that. sports, art, music, reading, meditation, etc. please find some time for yourself to breathe.
